expectations.text: Chooses an appropriate diagram type (flowchart/sequence/state) for the input shape
expectations.evidence: pipeline-after-first-run.md line 22 opens the fenced block with `flowchart TD`. The input.json is a DAG of six stages connected by directional edges (checkout -> build -> docker -> push -> deploy -> smoke) with `"type": "flowchart"`, so a top-down flowchart is the correct selection over sequence or state.

expectations.text: Handles nodes with quotes and special characters via safe escaping
expectations.evidence: Line 23 renders the `Checkout "main" branch` label as `checkout["Checkout #quot;main#quot; branch"]`, using the `#quot;` HTML-entity escape for the nested double-quotes inside the bracketed label. mermaid-lint.txt shows `node skills/wiki/scripts/mermaid_lint.js --page pipeline.md` returned `[]` with exit 0, confirming the diagram parses cleanly and bracket balance is preserved. The `&` in `Build & test` (line 24) is left literal — acceptable inside a Mermaid `["..."]` string label.

expectations.text: Updates pipeline.md idempotently (re-running on the same input produces no diff)
expectations.evidence: idempotency-check.txt reports both runs sha256 = 2e65ee9d75f08ebc0519546ebd8d2af8f8a1518a8382609f7a77217a4a155089 and `diff` returned no output. Independent verification: `diff pipeline-after-first-run.md pipeline-after-second-run.md` exits 0, and my own `shasum -a 256` on both files produced the identical hash. The agent's `injectMermaid` helper replaces the `## Diagrams` section in place rather than appending.

expectations.text: Never mutates wiki pages outside the specified target
expectations.evidence: scope-check.md documents `git status --short` showing only the pre-existing untracked `wiki-workspace/iteration-2/` directory, `git diff --stat HEAD` empty (no tracked files changed), and a `find -newer /tmp/eval-mermaid-flow/input.json -name '*.md'` (excluding node_modules, wiki-workspace, .git) returning zero results. The only markdown file written was `/tmp/eval-mermaid-flow/pipeline.md`, the explicit `--page` target, with mutation confined to the `## Diagrams` section.

claims.claim: The agent selected flowchart TD (top-down) orientation
claims.evidence: Line 22 of pipeline-after-first-run.md contains `flowchart TD`. TD is a reasonable default for a linear 6-stage pipeline.

claims.claim: The `#quot;` escape is the correct Mermaid-safe way to encode nested double-quotes inside a bracketed label
claims.evidence: mermaid_lint.js parsed the output with zero issues (exit 0, `[]`). Mermaid's documented escape mechanism for embedded quotes in `["..."]` labels is the `#quot;` HTML-entity form, which is what was emitted.

claims.claim: The injectMermaid helper replaces the Diagrams section in place rather than appending
claims.evidence: Second run produced a byte-identical file (same sha256, empty diff). If the helper appended instead of replaced, the second run would have duplicated the fenced block and produced a different hash.

claims.claim: All page content outside the `## Diagrams` section was preserved byte-for-byte
claims.evidence: Comparing pipeline-before.md lines 1-17 and 22-27 with pipeline-after-first-run.md lines 1-17 and 36-41: frontmatter, intro paragraph, `## Overview` section, and `## Operational notes` section are byte-identical. Only the placeholder comment under `## Diagrams` was replaced by the fenced mermaid block.

claims.claim: Zero tracked files in the repo were modified during the eval
claims.evidence: scope-check.md captures `git diff --stat HEAD` as empty and `git status --short` showing only the pre-existing untracked output directory. The agent operated entirely on `/tmp/eval-mermaid-flow/pipeline.md`, outside the repo tree.

suggestions.assertion: Chooses an appropriate diagram type (flowchart/sequence/state) for the input shape
suggestions.reason: The input.json hard-codes `"type": "flowchart"`, so the agent doesn't actually have to *choose* anything — it just honors the explicit type field. The assertion would also pass for a trivial passthrough. To make this discriminating, consider an eval variant where the input has no explicit type and the agent must infer flowchart vs sequence vs state from the edge/message shape (e.g. messages between actors would imply sequence; transition labels would imply state).

suggestions.assertion: Handles nodes with quotes and special characters via safe escaping
suggestions.reason: Only one special-character case is exercised (nested double-quote). The agent's escaping story for `<`, `>`, `|`, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, backticks, and leading `--` strings is untested by this fixture. Consider adding a node label like `List [a, b] | filter(x) -> y` to exercise the rest of the escape table.

The idempotency check only covers two consecutive runs with identical input. No assertion verifies that running with a *different* input correctly replaces (not appends) the previous block, which is the more interesting idempotency invariant for a long-lived page. Consider a two-run variant where run 2 has a new edge or node.

eval_feedback.overall: All four assertions pass with solid evidence. The main gap is that each assertion tests a single easy case; a more discriminating eval would exercise type-inference (no explicit `type` field), broader character classes, and replace-not-append under changing input.
